So I decided to start gardening this spring, and let me tell you, I had no idea what I was getting into! I thought you just stuck some seeds in the dirt and waited. Ha! That's adorable. Turns out there's soil pH and sun exposure and drainage and about a million other things I'd never thought about. My tomato plants died within the first week. Just completely gave up on life. My neighbor, who's got this incredible garden that looks like something from a magazine, came over and very politely told me I was overwatering everything. Apparently you can love your plants too much? Who knew! She gave me some tips and honestly she's been a lifesaver. My basil is actually growing now and I'm unreasonably proud of it. I showed my mom a photo and she was like, "that's nice, honey" in that voice that means she's not impressed at all. But whatever, I grew that basil! With my own hands! Well, and a lot of YouTube tutorials. But still! Next year I'm going for peppers. Dream big, right?
